routing: Definite English omissions/mistranslations found during the independent final review, returned to the chapter owner (bc-54ef0ff8-01f5-4d4d-8b50-9835f376f5c9) for application with the held identity/chronology corrections. Not an identity or date report; grants no approval.

chapterRepairs.before: Serving as advance registry clerk in the personnel directorate he was rebuked and removed from office; again for visiting the mansion of Prince of Guangning he was sentenced to several dozen strokes of the horsewhip.
chapterRepairs.after: Because he put forward a registry clerk to the personnel directorate he was rebuked and removed from office; again for visiting the mansion of Prince of Guangning he was sentenced to several dozen strokes of the horsewhip.
chapterRepairs.reason: 為進典籖於吏部: 為 = "because of"; he was censured for recommending a registry clerk (典籤) to the Ministry of Personnel. He never held a clerk post (he was a former minister and governor).

chapterRepairs.before: As advance registry clerk in the personnel directorate he was rebuked and dismissed; for visiting the Prince of Guangning's mansion he was also sentenced to several dozen horsewhip strokes.
chapterRepairs.after: For putting forward a registry clerk to the personnel directorate he was rebuked and dismissed; for visiting the Prince of Guangning's mansion he was also sentenced to several dozen horsewhip strokes.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same mistranslation in the idiomatic field.

chapterRepairs.before: Advanced to left grand master of splendid happiness, attended at the Wenslin Hall, and supervised compilation of the Imperial Overview.
chapterRepairs.after: Advanced to left grand master of splendid happiness, attended at the Wenlin Hall, and supervised compilation of the Imperial Overview.
chapterRepairs.reason: 文林館 is the Wenlin Hall; "Wenslin" is a misspelling.

chapterRepairs.before: He was advanced to left grand master of splendid happiness, attended at the Wenslin Hall, and supervised compilation of the Imperial Overview.
chapterRepairs.after: He was advanced to left grand master of splendid happiness, attended at the Wenlin Hall, and supervised compilation of the Imperial Overview.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same misspelling.

chapterRepairs.before: The households of Jishu and the rest, men and women, were sent to the northern marches; wives, daughters, and daughters-in-law were assigned to tribal wardens, young sons cast into the silkworm chamber, and property confiscated.
chapterRepairs.after: The households of Jishu and the rest, men and women, were sent to the northern marches; wives, daughters, and daughters-in-law were consigned to the Xiguan office of palace bondservants, young sons cast into the silkworm chamber, and property confiscated.
chapterRepairs.reason: 配奚官 = enslaved to the 奚官 (palace bondservant office); "tribal wardens" is a mistranslation.

chapterRepairs.before: The households of Jishu and the others, men and women, were sent north; wives, daughters, and daughters-in-law were assigned to tribal wardens, young sons to the silkworm chamber, and property was confiscated.
chapterRepairs.after: The households of Jishu and the others, men and women, were sent north; wives, daughters, and daughters-in-law were consigned to the palace bondservant office (Xiguan), young sons to the silkworm chamber, and property was confiscated.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same mistranslation.

chapterRepairs.before: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of the former minister over the masses Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, born of the former Wei Emperor Jing's aunt, the Great Princess of Boling.
chapterRepairs.after: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of the former Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, born of the former Wei Emperor Jing's aunt, the Great Princess of Boling.
chapterRepairs.reason: 故尚書令 = former Director of the Masters of Writing (as rendered at s0148); "Minister over the Masses" is 司徒, a different office.

chapterRepairs.before: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of former Minister over the Masses Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, child of Emperor Jing's aunt, the great Princess of Boling.
chapterRepairs.after: Staff officer Yuan Jingxian was son of former Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Shijun; his wife was daughter of Sima Qingyun, child of Emperor Jing's aunt, the great Princess of Boling.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same wrong office.

chapterRepairs.before: Ting also threw himself on Chief Registry Clerk Lu Zixian, who held acting military staff duties, and together they drew up plans; at the time of requesting grain he had Zixian proclaim the order, and ten cartloads of granary grain were issued—caught by a colleague and sent for trial.
chapterRepairs.after: Ting also threw himself on Lu Zixian, a staff officer acting as registry clerk, and together they drew up plans; at the time of requesting grain he had Zixian proclaim the order, and ten cartloads of granary grain were issued—caught by a colleague and sent for trial.
chapterRepairs.reason: 參軍事攝典簽 = staff officer (參軍事) acting as (攝) registry clerk (典簽); the two posts were reversed.

chapterRepairs.before: Ting also attached himself to chief registry clerk Lu Zixian, acting military staff officer, and they plotted together; when grain was requested Zixian proclaimed the order, ten cartloads were issued, and colleagues seized them for trial.
chapterRepairs.after: Ting also attached himself to Lu Zixian, a staff officer acting as registry clerk, and they plotted together; when grain was requested Zixian proclaimed the order, ten cartloads were issued, and colleagues seized them for trial.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same reversal.

chapterRepairs.before: Unrestrained by nature, he once drank at the home of Governor of Jiao province Sima Shiyun and hid two bronze mirrors.
chapterRepairs.after: Unrestrained by nature, he once drank at the home of Governor of Jiao province Sima Shiyun and hid two bronze plates.
chapterRepairs.reason: 銅疊 = bronze dishes/plates (疊 = 碟), not mirrors.

chapterRepairs.before: Unrestrained by nature, he once drank at Jiao governor Sima Shiyun home and hid two bronze mirrors.
chapterRepairs.after: Unrestrained by nature, he once drank at Jiao governor Sima Shiyun's home and hid two bronze plates.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same mistranslation; possessive restored.

chapterRepairs.before: When Gao Cheng met disaster Yuankang wounds were grave; he had Ting compose a letter entrusting family burdens, and also said, "At the border Zu Xi has a little property—take it soon."
chapterRepairs.after: When Gao Cheng met disaster Yuankang's wounds were grave; he had Ting compose a letter entrusting family burdens, and also said, "Zu Xi is holding a few things of mine; they should be retrieved soon."
chapterRepairs.reason: 祖喜邊有少許物 = "with Zu Xi (祖喜邊) there are a few things"; 邊 is "beside/with", not a frontier.

chapterRepairs.before: When Gao Cheng was killed Yuankang wounds were grave; he had Ting write a letter entrusting family matters, and also said, "Zu Xi at the border has a little property—take it soon."
chapterRepairs.after: When Gao Cheng was killed Yuankang's wounds were grave; he had Ting write a letter entrusting family matters, and also said, "Zu Xi is holding a few things of mine—retrieve them soon."
chapterRepairs.reason: Same mistranslation.

chapterRepairs.before: Zu Xi bore a grudge and thereupon informed Yuan Kang's two younger brothers, Shu Chen and Ji Ji, and the others.
chapterRepairs.after: Zu Xi bore a grudge and thereupon informed Yuankang's two younger brothers, Shu Chen and Ji Qu, and the others.
chapterRepairs.reason: 元康 is Chen Yuankang (given name, as elsewhere in the chapter), not a surname Yuan; 季璩 is Ji Qu (as in the idiomatic field).

chapterRepairs.before: Zu Xi nursed a grudge and told Yuan Kang's younger brothers Shu Chen and Ji Qu, among others.
chapterRepairs.after: Zu Xi nursed a grudge and told Yuankang's younger brothers Shu Chen and Ji Qu, among others.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same name error.

chapterRepairs.before: When it came to light, Wenxuan entrusted Attendant of the Masters of Writing Wang Tuya to investigate, and also wrote to Prince of Pingyang Yan, ordering him to take Ting into custody and not allow escape.
chapterRepairs.after: When it came to light, Wenxuan entrusted Gentleman Attendant of the headquarters Wang Tuya to investigate, and also wrote to Duke of Pingyang Yan, ordering him to take Ting into custody and not allow escape.
chapterRepairs.reason: 從事中郎 is a headquarters staff gentleman of Wenxuan's chancellery, not an attendant of the Masters of Writing; 平陽公 is a duke (公), not a prince (王).

chapterRepairs.before: When the theft came to light, Wenxuan put Attendant of the Masters of Writing Wang Tuya in charge of the inquiry and wrote Prince of Pingyang Yan as well, telling him to take Ting into custody and allow no escape.
chapterRepairs.after: When the theft came to light, Wenxuan put Gentleman Attendant of the headquarters Wang Tuya in charge of the inquiry and wrote Duke of Pingyang Yan as well, telling him to take Ting into custody and allow no escape.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same errors.

chapterRepairs.before: Ting was skilled at making walnut oil for painting and presented it to the Prince of Changgang, saying, "Your Highness has extraordinary bone structure; Xiao Zheng dreamed that Your Highness rode a dragon into heaven."
chapterRepairs.after: Ting was skilled at making walnut oil for painting and presented it to the Prince of Changguang, saying, "Your Highness has extraordinary bone structure; Xiaozheng dreamed that Your Highness rode a dragon into heaven."
chapterRepairs.reason: 長廣王 = Prince of Changguang; 孝徵 is Zu Ting's style Xiaozheng (as in the idiomatic field).

chapterRepairs.before: The prince said to him, "If that is so, then my elder brother ought to grow very rich."
chapterRepairs.after: The prince said to him, "If that is so, I ought to make you, elder brother, greatly rich and noble."
chapterRepairs.reason: 當使兄大富貴: 使 is causative and 兄 is the prince's polite address to Zu Ting ("brother"); the reigning emperor, his actual elder brother, could not be "made rich". He rewarded Ting on accession (s0125).

chapterRepairs.before: The prince said, "If that is so, my elder brother should grow very rich indeed."
chapterRepairs.after: The prince said, "If that is so, I shall make you, brother, greatly rich and honored."
chapterRepairs.reason: Same mistranslation.

chapterRepairs.before: Ting now toed the emperor's wishes memorialized to posthumously honor Grand Ancestor as Emperor Shenwu and change High Ancestor Emperor Wenxuan's title to Weizong Jinglie Emperor, to please Wucheng; the emperor assented.
chapterRepairs.after: Ting now played to the emperor's wishes and memorialized to posthumously honor Grand Ancestor Emperor Xianwu as Emperor Shenwu and change High Ancestor Emperor Wenxuan's title to Weizong Jinglie Emperor, to please Wucheng; the emperor assented.
chapterRepairs.reason: The literal field omits 獻武皇帝 (Emperor Xianwu) and is ungrammatical.

chapterRepairs.before: He had earlier been friendly with Secretariat Attendant Liu Ti; he therefore memorialized the crimes of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing Zhao Yanshen, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director Yuan Wenyao, and Attendant-in-Ordinary He Shikai, ordering Ti to present the memorial.
chapterRepairs.after: He had earlier been friendly with Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate Liu Ti; he therefore memorialized the crimes of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing Zhao Yanshen, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director Yuan Wenyao, and Attendant-in-Ordinary He Shikai, ordering Ti to present the memorial.
chapterRepairs.reason: 黃門侍郎 belongs to the Chancellery (門下), not the Secretariat (中書); the chapter renders it "gentleman of the yellow gate" at s0013.

chapterRepairs.before: He had been friendly with secretariat attendant Liu Ti. He now memorialized the crimes of attendant-in-ordinary and director of the masters of writing Zhao Yanshen, attendant-in-ordinary and left vice director Yuan Wenyao, and attendant-in-ordinary He Shikai, and told Ti to present it.
chapterRepairs.after: He had been friendly with gentleman attendant of the yellow gate Liu Ti. He now memorialized the crimes of attendant-in-ordinary and director of the masters of writing Zhao Yanshen, attendant-in-ordinary and left vice director Yuan Wenyao, and attendant-in-ordinary He Shikai, and told Ti to present it.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same wrong office.

chapterRepairs.before: Ting therefore sent a letter to Dame Lu's younger brother Sida, saying, "Zhao Yanshen's heart is deep and hidden; he wishes to perform the Yi and Huo deed—the Lady's brother and sister, how can they be secure? Why not early employ a man of counsel?"
chapterRepairs.after: Ting therefore sent a letter to Dame Lu's younger brother Sida, saying, "Zhao Yanshen's heart is deep and hidden; he wishes to perform the Yi and Huo deed—you, the Ceremonial Peer, and your elder sister—how can you be secure? Why not early employ a man of counsel?"
chapterRepairs.reason: 儀同姊弟 addresses Sida (a 儀同) and his elder sister Lu Lingxuan; 姊弟 is "elder sister and younger brother", not the lady's siblings.

chapterRepairs.before: Ting sent a letter to Dame Lu's younger brother Sida: "Zhao Yanshen's heart runs deep and hidden. He means to play Yi Yin and Huo Guang—the lady's brother and sister, how will they stay safe? Why not take a clever man into counsel early?"
chapterRepairs.after: Ting sent a letter to Dame Lu's younger brother Sida: "Zhao Yanshen's heart runs deep and hidden. He means to play Yi Yin and Huo Guang—you, the Ceremonial Peer, and your elder sister—how will you stay safe? Why not take a clever man into counsel early?"
chapterRepairs.reason: Same mistranslation.

chapterRepairs.before: The edict required a confirming memorial; the signature of Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulu Xiaqing was to be obtained.
chapterRepairs.after: The edict required a confirming memorial; the signature of Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulü Xiaoqing was to be obtained.
chapterRepairs.reason: 斛律孝卿: 孝 is xiào; Hulü as elsewhere in the chapter (Hulü Guang).

chapterRepairs.before: The edict had to be confirmed by memorial, with the signature of attendant-in-ordinary Hulu Xiaqing.
chapterRepairs.after: The edict had to be confirmed by memorial, with the signature of attendant-in-ordinary Hulü Xiaoqing.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same romanization error.

chapterRepairs.before: Xiaqing secretly told Gao Yuanhai; Yuanhai said to Hou Lü Fen and Mu Tipo, "Xiaozheng is a Han fellow, and both his eyes cannot even see things — how could he be fit to command the guards?"
chapterRepairs.after: Xiaoqing secretly told Gao Yuanhai; Yuanhai said to Hou Lü Fen and Mu Tipo, "Xiaozheng is a Han fellow, and both his eyes cannot even see things — how could he be fit to command the guards?"
chapterRepairs.reason: 孝卿 = Xiaoqing.

chapterRepairs.before: Xiaqing secretly warned Gao Yuanhai. Yuanhai told Hou Lü Fen and Mu Tipo, "Xiaozheng is a Han man, and his eyes can barely make out a thing — how is he fit to command the guards?"
chapterRepairs.after: Xiaoqing secretly warned Gao Yuanhai. Yuanhai told Hou Lü Fen and Mu Tipo, "Xiaozheng is a Han man, and his eyes can barely make out a thing — how is he fit to command the guards?"
chapterRepairs.reason: Same romanization error.

chapterRepairs.before: Ting therefore prompted Vice Director of the Censorate Li Boju to impeach Chief Clerk Wang Zichong for taking bribes, knowing the case would implicate Mu Tipo; he wished guilt by bribery to spread, hoping thereby to bring them down together with Lu Matron.
chapterRepairs.after: Ting therefore prompted Vice Director of the Censorate Li Bolü to impeach Chief Clerk Wang Zichong for taking bribes, knowing the case would implicate Mu Tipo; he wished guilt by bribery to spread, hoping thereby to bring them down together with Lu Matron.
chapterRepairs.reason: 麗伯侓: 侓 is read lù (repository glossary); the parallels Beishi 47 and Zizhi tongjian 171 write 麗伯律 (lǜ). "ju" is unsupported.

chapterRepairs.before: Ting therefore nudged vice director of the censorate Li Boju to impeach chief clerk Wang Zichong for bribery, knowing the case would rope in Mu Tipo — he meant the taint of graft to spread and pull Lu Matron down with them.
chapterRepairs.after: Ting therefore nudged vice director of the censorate Li Bolü to impeach chief clerk Wang Zichong for bribery, knowing the case would rope in Mu Tipo — he meant the taint of graft to spread and pull Lu Matron down with them.
chapterRepairs.reason: Same romanization error.
